transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because the doctor doing my insurance physical said my weight was too low. I mean, I just see myself as lean—from being on ladders and working long days—but they thought I should get it checked out.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yeah, I guess so. If the scale goes up even a little—like after a client dinner or eating bread—I get tense about it. Then the next day I cut back so it doesn’t stick.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as overweight?

I don’t know if I’d say overweight exactly, but when I catch myself in a mirror—or in photos by one of my murals—I focus on whether my stomach and face look sharp enough. It kind of sets the tone for the whole day.
Do you ever eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period and feel like you can’t stop?
No, I haven’t really noticed that. I usually keep pretty close track of what I eat.
Have you ever made yourself vomit to keep from gaining weight?
No, I haven’t done that.
Aside from vomiting, have you used laxatives, diuretics, or enemas to try to prevent weight gain?
No, I haven’t used anything like that.
Have you had episodes where you ate a very large amount of food within a short period of time?
No, I don't think I've had that happen. I tend to be pretty aware of how much I'm eating.
Have you been deliberately eating less than your body needs in order to keep your weight low?
Yeah. Most days it’s just coffee, maybe a protein bar between paint jobs, and a small dinner. A full meal feels like it would slow me down.
Have you ever had times when you ate what felt like a large amount of food and then tried to get rid of it afterward?
I’m not sure what you mean by a large amount. I haven’t really had times where I ate a lot and then did something afterward to get rid of it.
Do you ever exercise excessively to prevent weight gain?
I’m not sure what counts as excessive. I’m on my feet a lot for work, but I don’t really think of that as exercise.
Do you ever intentionally go for long periods without eating to prevent weight gain?
Yeah, I mean, I’ll go most of the day without eating. It’s usually just coffee, maybe a protein bar while I’m working, then a small dinner. A full meal during the day feels like it’d slow me down.
Do you ever exercise specifically to burn calories or keep from gaining weight?
Not really. I’m active at work, but I’m not doing extra workouts with calories or weight in mind.
What is your current height and weight?
I don’t have the exact numbers offhand. The doctor at my insurance physical said my weight was too low, but I’ve always just thought I looked lean from being on ladders and working long days.
What is the lowest weight you’ve been at recently?
I’m not sure of the number. The insurance doctor said it was too low, but I honestly just thought I looked lean from being on ladders and working long days.
Have you ever had an episode where you ate an unusually large amount of food in a short time and felt unable to stop?
I’m not really sure what counts as unusually large. I eat regular meals when I eat, but I haven’t noticed times where I felt like I couldn’t stop.
Has any doctor told you that your weight is significantly below what is considered normal for your height?
Yes. The doctor who did my insurance physical said my weight was too low for me. I just thought I was lean from all the climbing and long workdays.
Have there been times when you ate a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar period?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I eat normal portions when I do eat—I haven’t had a time where I ate a huge amount compared to other people.
